subject: SolaceAI performance qualification & PoC scope

Subject: Recap + clarifying SLOs from today's call

Hi Lina — great to meet the SolaceAI team today. Short recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the PoC: 

Quick recap (from our notes)
- Primary objective: validate that Redwood can meet SolaceAI's interactive latency SLOs at production scale for your summarization+generation pipeline.
- Typical request profile: user prompt + retrieval context => 6k–10k input tokens, expected output ~512 tokens for summaries and up to 2048 for longer generations.
- Streaming requirement: you need first-token streaming start within the p95 SLO (so UX shows text immediately) and a steady per-token rate for the remainder of the response.
- Concurrency & throughput: baseline concurrency per tenant ~30 concurrent sessions, expected steady QPS 10–12, spikes to ~45 QPS during peak campaigns.
- Security: you asked to confirm isolation options (dedicated pool / VPC) and audit logs.

Clarifying Qs for scoping PoC
1) Can you confirm the most common input size (median) vs. the 95th percentile input size? We recorded median ~3.5k tokens and 95th ~9k tokens — is that accurate?
2) For streaming, is the UX requirement that the first token appears within 250ms p95, or is a slightly larger first-byte preferred as long as the first few tokens stream without large gaps?
3) Any hard limits on output tokens (max response length)? We noted some workflows need up to 2k, others only 512.

Next steps
- We'll draft a two-week PoC plan (dedicated canary capacity + runbook + success criteria) and share it by EOD tomorrow. Attached is a skeleton we typically start from.
- If procurement needs an NDA/SOW to proceed, loop them in and we'll expedite.

Attachments: [attachment: redwood_poc_plan_v2.pdf (pdf, 420KB)]

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Recap + clarifying SLOs from today's call

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token distributions
- Median input: ~3,000–4,000 tokens (we typically truncate retrieval results for UI flows).
- 95th percentile: ~12,000 tokens for extended thread summarization jobs (rare, ~2–3% of requests).

2) Streaming / latency expectations
- Target: first token visible within 200–300ms p95 is what product wants. That said, for the long-context jobs we prioritize a predictable start + steady streaming rate rather than super-fast first byte. If you can guarantee the first token by 300ms and then streaming at ~60–90 tokens/sec, that's acceptable.

3) Output limits
- Hard cap from us: 4,096 tokens for generation. Typical summary flows use 256–512. Suite of longer generation tasks can go to 2k but we'll enforce quotas per endpoint.

4) Traffic patterns
- Steady: 8–12 QPS across tenants for classification/summaries.
- Bursts: up to 50 QPS for short windows (10–15 minutes) during product launches.

5) Compliance
- NDA in place; procurement will send a standard security questionnaire after we confirm PoC scope.

We can proceed with the PoC you outline. Please include a specific metric for streaming-first-byte p95 and an acceptance run with representative 95th-percentile payloads.

Thanks — Lina

Subject: Re: Recap + clarifying SLOs from today's call

Thanks — looping back with a proposed technical approach for the PoC and success criteria so everyone has clarity.

Proposed PoC scope (2 weeks)- Environment: Dedicated canary pool (NVidia H100 / customer VPC option available)- Models: curated open LLM (quantized runtime) + fallback to smaller variant for very high-load scenarios- Workloads to run: median flow (3k–4k tokens, summary 512 tok), 95th flow (9k–12k input, output up to 2k)- Traffic profile: steady 12 QPS + two 15-minute burst windows up to 45–50 QPS

Key engineering work
- Measure streaming-first-byte latency (time to first token) and per-token emission rate.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated retrievals to reduce compute on hot prefixes.
- Run concurrency tests with 30–60 concurrent sessions to see p95 degradation curves.
- Instrument detailed traces (per-request token times) and cost-per-token breakdowns.

Success criteria (pass/fail)
- Streaming-first-byte p95 <= 300ms for median flows (3k–4k in).
- Streaming-first-byte p95 <= 500ms for 95th percentile (9k–12k in).
- Sustained per-token emission >= 60 tokens/sec for generated output in streaming mode.
- System maintains 95% of single-tenant throughput (no more than 20% degradation) under burst profile when using dedicated pool.

Deliverables- Runbook + test harness (shared Drive).
- PoC report: latency histograms, traces, cost estimates, recommended config (batching, quantization, autoscale policy).

Risks & mitigations- Large KV cache sizes may increase memory footprint; mitigation: eviction policy + aggressive prefix hashing.
- Very long-context 95th percentile may push latency higher; mitigation: recommend soft-truncation with retrieval ranker and show fallback options (partial context + follow-up generation).

Action items
- Marissa: confirm SOW/procurement path and if procurement wants the security questionnaire now.
- Aisha: I'll schedule the load tests and share the test harness links.
- Lina: confirm if the 500ms p95 for 95th percentile is acceptable as a PoC threshold; we can iterate on tuning and deployment shape.
